verdict.rationale: Warp ships documented CLI/IPC surfaces — the standalone Warp Agent CLI (works in any terminal, over SSH, creates its own PTY, can run/control full-screen apps) and the Oz CLI for running/managing cloud agents from scripts or CI with API-key auth — giving real command-line scriptability of agent sessions. However, the evidence is agent-centric (starting conversations, running commands, controlling processes) rather than direct terminal-window primitives like opening/arranging windows or querying pane/window state as the story literally describes (tmux/iTerm2-style control). Missing for 10: explicit documented commands to open/manage Warp windows or panes, send raw text to a specific pane, or query terminal UI state independent of an agent session; independent hands-on confirmation of such scripting.
